workers.title: Worker bootstrap credentials
workers.description: Create short-lived bootstrap credentials for native workers that still use the SmartAIHub control plane. Hermes, Claude Code, and Codex should use MCP & Connected Devices for tool access.
workers.connectionBoundary.title: Choose the correct connection
workers.connectionBoundary.description: Worker bootstrap credentials and MCP credentials are different. MCP & Connected Devices is the primary path for Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and other MCP clients. Keep this page only for native worker registration, heartbeat, job claim/report, or legacy runtimes that do not support MCP directly.
workers.connectionBoundary.mcpDescriptio: Use the canonical Streamable HTTP endpoint with OAuth/device approval. For a machine without a browser, create a dedicated MCP CLI key in API Keys and apply its credit budgets there.
workers.connectionBoundary.bootstrapDesc: This key registers a worker and carries its control-plane policy. It is not an MCP token and must not be pasted into Hermes, Claude, Codex, or an MCP Authorization header.
workers.connectionBoundary.neverUseAsMcp: Do not use this key as an MCP credential.
workers.mcpMethods.title: How each worker reaches MCP
workers.mcpMethods.description: Use MCP & Connected Devices whenever the runtime supports remote Streamable HTTP. Use a worker bootstrap key only for the worker control plane; use the separate Remotion Executor enrollment for local rendering.
workers.mcpMethods.hermes.method: MCP OAuth/device; bootstrap only for native worker registration
workers.mcpMethods.hermes.description: Hermes One and Hermes CLI connect to /v1/mcp with OAuth. A Hermes worker that also registers, heartbeats, claims, or reports jobs still needs its worker bootstrap flow.
workers.mcpMethods.openclaw.method: MCP if supported; otherwise worker bootstrap
workers.mcpMethods.openclaw.description: Configure /v1/mcp with OAuth or a dedicated MCP CLI key when the OpenClaw build supports Streamable HTTP. If it only supports the worker control plane, use this page for registration and enable delegate:mcp only when the delegated job requires it.
workers.mcpMethods.zeroclaw.method: MCP if supported; device enrollment for the native worker
workers.mcpMethods.zeroclaw.description: Use /v1/mcp for tools when the desktop runtime has an MCP client. Keep device/worker enrollment separate for heartbeat, job claim, upload, and machine-bound execution.
workers.mcpMethods.nemoclaw.method: MCP through the sandbox gateway, or worker bootstrap
workers.mcpMethods.nemoclaw.description: A sandbox may call /v1/mcp only through its approved outbound gateway and tenant policy. If the sandbox exposes only worker registration, use the bootstrap key and do not put it in MCP configuration.
workers.mcpMethods.hiclaw.method: MCP through the cluster gateway; bootstrap per worker pool
workers.mcpMethods.hiclaw.description: Point the cluster MCP gateway at /v1/mcp using OAuth or a dedicated MCP CLI key. Keep pool registration, heartbeat, and job leasing on the worker control-plane credential.
workers.mcpMethods.remotion.method: MCP for submit/status/cancel + separate Remotion Executor device
workers.mcpMethods.remotion.description: MCP submits and monitors Remotion jobs. The Windows/macOS machine that renders needs the signed Remotion Executor pack and device-bound connect/start flow; never substitute an MCP key for the executor credential.
workers.quickAccessDescription: Open the Workers tab to create registration keys, set permissions, choose a provider, and apply quotas.
workers.createDescription: Generate a short-lived worker bootstrap key. Keep the raw token secret and copy it only once.
workers.label: Key label
workers.expiryHint: Leave blank for a non-expiring key, or set a short lifespan for safer bootstrap.
workers.invalidExpiry: Enter a valid expiry day number, or leave it blank for no expiry.
workers.providerRequired: Pick a provider before creating a pinned worker key.
workers.copyNow: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again after you leave this screen.
workers.listDescription: Manage issued keys and revoke any token you no longer trust.
workers.guidanceBody: Create a key here, copy the token once, and paste it into the Hermes/OpenClaw worker bootstrap configuration. The selected provider pin travels with the token so {{tenantName}} can route the gateway deterministically.
workers.invalidQuota: Enter valid quota numbers, or leave the fields blank for unlimited usage.
workers.quotas.title: Worker control-plane budgets
workers.quotas.summary: Set optional credit caps for this native worker bootstrap key. These limits do not control MCP OAuth/device sessions; configure MCP CLI key quotas in API Keys.
workers.quotas.hint: These values map to the worker budget policy after registration. Empty means no cap for this worker key.
workers.quotas.tip1: Use a short-lived key for the first connection test, then extend the quota only after the worker is trusted.
workers.quotas.tip2: If the worker should never exceed a fixed budget, set the smallest hourly or daily cap that still lets it finish its job.
workers.quotas.tip3: For browserless MCP clients, do not reuse this key: create a dedicated MCP CLI key and set its 5-hour, daily, and weekly credit limits in API Keys.
workers.permissions.title: Permissions
workers.permissions.description: Pick a preset or switch to Custom to fine-tune scopes one by one.
workers.permissions.scopesHint: Click checkboxes to allow the worker to use specific gateway families and workspace features.
workers.permissions.summary: Permissions travel with the key and help {{tenantName}} decide what the worker may request after registration.
workers.permissions.tip1: Read-only keys are best for simple assistants and first-time setup.
workers.permissions.tip2: Use a pinned provider only when you need a specific backend for compatibility or policy reasons.
workers.permissions.tip3: Custom scopes should be the minimum set the worker actually needs.
workers.permissions.groups.gateway.title: Gateway and LLM
workers.permissions.groups.gateway.descr: Model calls, delegated HTTP, delegated MCP, and callbacks.
workers.permissions.groups.dramaMedia.de: Read, bind, scan, preprocess, and publish Drama Series media assets.
workers.permissions.groups.knowledge.des: Files, library access, and RAG read/write operations.
Allow the worker to execute skills or agent workflows.
workers.permissions.groups.workOs.title: Work OS
workers.permissions.groups.workOs.descri: Read or write work items and operating queues.
workers.connectedWorkers.title: Connected workers ({{count}})
workers.connectedWorkers.description: Review worker apps that have already connected, confirm the device details, and choose who can use each worker.
workers.connectedWorkers.shareDescriptio: Keep this worker private, share it with selected groups, or allow the whole tenant to use it.
workers.connectedWorkers.capabilitiesTit: What this Worker App can do
workers.connectedWorkers.workerPermissio: Choose what this Worker App may use. Because this worker has no device authorization record yet, these permissions will be applied when it reconnects and completes approval.
workers.connectedWorkers.permissionsDesc: Uncheck an approved scope to revoke it on this device. New scopes require reconnecting and approving the Worker App again.
workers.connectedWorkers.cannotGrantMore: This editor can reduce approved permissions only. To grant more, reconnect the Worker App and approve the additional scopes.
workers.connectedWorkers.deviceRecordMis: No device record is available; reconnect this Worker App to manage its permissions.
workers.connectedWorkers.noGroups: No groups available for sharing yet.
workers.connectedWorkers.shareModes.priv: Only your own jobs can use this worker.
workers.connectedWorkers.shareModes.grou: Jobs from members of the selected groups can use this worker.
workers.connectedWorkers.shareModes.tena: Any eligible user in this tenant can use this worker.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.r: Best for safe first-time registration with minimal access.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.o: Adds delegation and publish rights for normal operations.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.c: Good for content generation and media-heavy workflows.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.k: Optimized for library, RAG, and knowledge-centric work.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.w: Focused on work intake, queues, and operating tasks.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.v: For local Drama Series media scanning, preprocessing, and publishing.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.f: All supported scopes for a power-user worker.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.c: Manually choose only the scopes you want.
workers.guide.step1: Choose the worker type, then decide whether the LLM should auto-select a provider or stay pinned to one provider.
workers.guide.step2: Pick a permission preset, then refine the allowed scopes if the preset is not exact enough.
workers.guide.step3: Set hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly credit caps only when you want to limit usage; leave any field blank for unlimited.
workers.guide.step4: Create the key, copy the token once, and paste it into the Hermes/OpenClaw bootstrap flow.
workers.guide.step5: Revoke the key any time if the token is leaked, no longer needed, or should not be used again.
workers.safety.title: Safety checklist
workers.safety.tip1: Use short expiries for temporary setup keys.
workers.safety.tip2: Prefer the smallest permission set that still lets the worker do the job.
workers.safety.tip3: Pin a provider only when deterministic routing matters.
workers.safety.tip4: Revoke unused keys regularly and review the audit trail after registration.
workers.connect.title: How to connect the worker
workers.connect.description: After you create the key, open the worker's own bootstrap or registration screen, paste the token into its registration field, and start the worker once.
workers.connect.hermes.title: Hermes
workers.connect.hermes.description: Use Hermes when the bridge is managed by the Hermes runtime and you want {{tenantName}} to own policy and credits.
workers.connect.hermes.step1: Open the Hermes container or bridge setup and choose the registration/bootstrap flow.
workers.connect.hermes.step2: Paste the worker access token into the registration token field and keep the provider pin if you selected one.
workers.connect.hermes.step3: Finish setup, then check Admin Monitoring to confirm the worker registered successfully.
workers.connect.openclaw.title: OpenClaw
workers.connect.openclaw.description: Use OpenClaw when the worker already knows how to register with the {{tenantName}} control plane.
workers.connect.openclaw.step1: Open the OpenClaw worker bootstrap or enrollment screen.
workers.connect.openclaw.step2: Paste the token into the worker registration key or bootstrap token field.
workers.connect.openclaw.step3: Start the worker, then bind it to a team if you want it to receive team work.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.title: ZeroClaw
workers.connect.zeroclaw.description: Use ZeroClaw for desktop-managed workers that connect from a device you control.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step1: Open the ZeroClaw desktop or device enrollment flow.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step2: Paste the token into the registration key field and save the device identity if prompted.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step3: Complete enrollment and verify the worker appears online in monitoring.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.title: NemoClaw
workers.connect.nemoclaw.description: Use NemoClaw for sandboxed workers that register into a secure pool.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step1: Open the NemoClaw sandbox registration or pool bootstrap screen.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step2: Paste the token into the sandbox registration field before the first start.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step3: Launch the sandbox and confirm the worker enters the expected pool in monitoring.
connectedDevices.title: MCP & Connected Devices
connectedDevices.description: Review the devices and MCP sessions that have access to your account. Remote MCP does not require a download.
connectedDevices.workerSummaryDescriptio: These are Worker App devices connected with your own account. Open a Worker App card below to inspect its granted, allowed, and effective functions.
connectedDevices.remoteMcpDescription: Connect Hermes or another MCP client to SmartAIHub over HTTPS. Local Remotion installation is optional.
connectedDevices.oauthReadinessUnavailab: OAuth discovery is not ready on this server yet. An administrator must save Admin → Infrastructure → MCP/OAuth and enable the tenant gates Modern MCP protocol, MCP documentation resources, OAuth Protected Resource Metadata, and MCP OAuth Authorization Server.
connectedDevices.legacyFallbackDescripti: Older Hermes or API-key clients continue to use the protected compatibility fallback. For a machine without a browser, create Settings → API Keys → Create MCP CLI Key and store it in the client's secret store; new clients should use OAuth discovery on this endpoint.
connectedDevices.helpTitle: Connect Hermes, Claude Code, or Codex
connectedDevices.helpDescription: Use the same SmartAIHub MCP endpoint. Choose your client below, complete OAuth in the browser, and approve only the permissions you understand.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionsDescript: OAuth approval is the maximum access for this device. The server checks tenant, ACL, quota, feature flags, and the device policy on every MCP request.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionStep1: Review the SmartAIHub tenant/workspace shown on the consent page.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionStep2: Approve only the scopes you need. Generate/media, library download, and Remotion render are write or file-access capabilities.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionStep3: After login, return to the client and reload tools. The visible tools are principal- and permission-scoped.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionStep4: To reduce access later, uncheck permissions on this device and save. To terminate the connection, use Revoke.
connectedDevices.helpPermissionScopeExam: Examples: read tools = mcp:read; generate media = media:generate; download files = media:download/library:download; render video = remotion:submit/remotion:read/remotion:cancel; Hermes control = hermes:connect/hermes:read/hermes:generate/hermes:disconnect.
connectedDevices.helpHermesCliDescriptio: Run these commands in PowerShell, Windows Terminal, or macOS Terminal. The first connection opens SmartAIHub OAuth; Hermes stores its own credentials.
connectedDevices.helpHermesVerify: A successful connection shows the server in the list and tools after authentication. If Hermes shows a Pydantic capability error, update Hermes and retry discovery; the server advertises capability objects, not boolean values.
connectedDevices.helpHermesOneDescriptio: Hermes One uses the desktop UI and the public hermes:// setup link. No API key or manual token copy is needed for OAuth.
connectedDevices.helpHermesOneStep1: Click Connect in Hermes One from the MCP & Devices page.
connectedDevices.helpHermesOneStep2: Confirm the SmartAIHub endpoint and choose OAuth.
connectedDevices.helpHermesOneStep3: Sign in in the browser and review the tenant and permissions.
connectedDevices.helpHermesOneStep4: Approve, return to Hermes One, and reload tools.
connectedDevices.helpExecutorNote: MCP connection lets Hermes submit and monitor permitted jobs. Real video rendering on this computer still requires the separate Remotion Executor: install the matching signed pack, run doctor, connect, and start. Its worker credential is separate from the MCP credential.
connectedDevices.helpClaudeDescription: Use Claude Code's remote HTTP MCP configuration. After adding the server, open /mcp in Claude Code and complete the browser consent flow.
connectedDevices.helpClaudeDesktopNote: For Claude Desktop's graphical Connector UI, use Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Do not put this remote server in claude_desktop_config.json; the Connector UI owns OAuth and its credential store.
connectedDevices.helpCodexDescription: Add SmartAIHub as a remote MCP server, complete OAuth when Codex opens the browser, then verify the server before starting a new session.
connectedDevices.helpCodexVerify: Use codex mcp list and then start or reload a Codex session. The final verification is successful tool discovery and a harmless read-only call.
connectedDevices.helpNoBrowserDescriptio: Create Settings → API Keys → Create MCP CLI Key first. Give it only the required scopes and credit budgets, store it in the OS secret store as SMARTAIHUB_MCP_KEY, and never paste the real key into chat, a committed file, or shell history.
connectedDevices.helpAfterConnect: After any client connects, verify tools/list and run a harmless read-only operation first. Rendering additionally needs the Remotion scopes, an approved executor, and a healthy local runtime pack.
connectedDevices.endpointCopyFailed: Could not copy the MCP endpoint
connectedDevices.cliSetupCopyFailed: Could not copy the Hermes CLI setup
connectedDevices.remotionExecutorDescrip: MCP connects Hermes, Claude, or Codex to SmartAIHub. To render on this computer, download the matching published signed pack, run its installer once, then run doctor, connect, and start. The executor uses device approval and keeps worker credentials separate from MCP.
connectedDevices.remotionExecutorSecurit: The executor uses a separate device-bound worker credential. Never paste an MCP token or worker token into chat.
connectedDevices.remotionRuntimeAvailabi: MCP connection and local video rendering are separate. Install only a published pack matching the computer; a missing pack means local rendering is not enabled for that target yet.
connectedDevices.moduleStatusDescription: Live checks for OAuth discovery, tenant gates, and the local Remotion runtime packs. HTTP 200 means the public endpoint responded; a disabled tenant flag intentionally blocks that capability.
connectedDevices.quotaDescription: Keep the quota with the credential type that actually uses it. MCP OAuth/device sessions, browserless MCP CLI keys, and native worker control-plane credentials are enforced separately.
connectedDevices.quotaOAuthDescription: No Worker Key is needed. The server applies the signed-in user's tenant credit and policy checks to every MCP call; reducing scopes or revoking this device takes effect immediately.
connectedDevices.quotaCliDescription: Create or edit the dedicated MCP CLI key in API Keys. Its 5-hour, 1-day, and 7-day credit budgets can be lowered, raised, or set unlimited per window.
connectedDevices.quotaWorkerDescription: Worker hourly/daily/weekly/monthly caps remain on the Worker bootstrap page because they become the worker control-plane budget after registration. They do not apply to MCP OAuth sessions.
connectedDevices.quickStartTitle: Choose how to connect your AI client
connectedDevices.quickStartDescription: Choose the client you already use. Hermes One can open its setup directly; Hermes CLI, Claude, Codex, and other clients use the same endpoint with browser OAuth. If the machine has no browser, use the dedicated MCP CLI key from Settings → API Keys.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesOne.title: Hermes One
connectedDevices.clients.hermesOne.step1: Click Connect in Hermes One when OAuth is ready.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesOne.step2: Confirm the public server configuration in Hermes.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesOne.step3: Sign in in the browser, approve permissions, then reload tools.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesCli.title: Hermes CLI / Agent
connectedDevices.clients.hermesCli.step1: Open PowerShell, Windows Terminal, or macOS Terminal.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesCli.step2: Run the OAuth setup commands from the guide.
connectedDevices.clients.hermesCli.step3: Complete browser login, then run test/list to verify tools.
connectedDevices.clients.claude.title: Claude / Claude Desktop
connectedDevices.clients.claude.step1: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
connectedDevices.clients.claude.step2: Enter this endpoint, then click Add and Connect.
connectedDevices.clients.claude.step3: Review permissions and enable only the tools you need.
connectedDevices.clients.codex.title: Codex
connectedDevices.clients.codex.step1: Add SmartAIHub as a remote MCP server.
connectedDevices.clients.codex.step2: Let Codex open the SmartAIHub sign-in page.
connectedDevices.clients.codex.step3: Approve access, then retry tool discovery.
connectedDevices.otherClients.title: Other MCP clients
connectedDevices.otherClients.descriptio: For another MCP client, choose remote Streamable HTTP and OAuth/browser login. Do not guess a static token header.
connectedDevices.otherClients.step1: Set the remote server URL to the endpoint shown below.
connectedDevices.otherClients.step2: Let the client discover OAuth metadata and open the browser.
connectedDevices.otherClients.step3: If it cannot do MCP OAuth, use an explicitly supported fallback or the REST/OpenAPI guide.
connectedDevices.fallbackTitle: If this client does not support OAuth
connectedDevices.fallbackDescription: Use an API key only for the documented REST/legacy compatibility path, or Hermes pairing where supported. It is not a universal MCP replacement for OAuth; never paste tokens into chat.
connectedDevices.deviceListDescription: Only devices approved by your account are shown here.
connectedDevices.loadFailed: Connected devices could not be loaded.
connectedDevices.empty: No MCP or local executor devices are connected.
connectedDevices.clientOriginVerifiedDes: This origin matched the callback registered for this OAuth client.
connectedDevices.clientOriginUnavailable: This is a device pairing or non-OAuth connection, so there is no registered browser callback origin.
connectedDevices.permissionPolicyDescrip: By default, every scope approved during OAuth is allowed. Uncheck a scope to block it for this device only; changes are enforced by the server immediately and can never add a scope that was not approved.
connectedDevices.workerPermissionPolicyD: The scopes issued during Worker App approval are the upper bound. Uncheck a scope to block it for this device immediately; enabling a scope requires that it was included in the original approval.
connectedDevices.permissionSaveHint: Save the changed permissions for this device.
connectedDevices.scopeDescriptionFallbac: Permission granted for the corresponding SmartAIHub capability.

connectedDevices.scopeDescription.mcp_wr: Use actions that change data or start operations.

connectedDevices.revokeDescription: This will stop {{name}} from refreshing, claiming jobs, using MCP write tools, and uploading artifacts.
connectedDevices.revokeFailed: Device access could not be revoked
connectedDevices.revokeAllDescription: This will revoke every OAuth and Hermes MCP connection belonging to this account in the current tenant. Other integrations and worker keys are not changed.
connectedDevices.revokeAllDisabled: There are no active MCP connections to revoke
connectedDevices.revokeAllFailed: MCP connections could not be revoked
